correctness.rationale: Proved five steps: an m-rough lower bound \(L_m(u)\ge c_m\sqrt{u}\) by local prime-power estimates; a zero second iterate on any bad residue class; the exact first-two-iterate identity and a uniform all-exponent abundance condition for sufficiently large good prime bases; CRT plus Dirichlet equidistribution to obtain exact delta_m; exhaustive symbolic treatment of m=2 and m=4 small exceptional prime bases, with strict inequalities for all positive exponents. A standalone exact-integer/rational script checks 1565 lemma instances, 609 branch cases and 488 special classifications without treating enumeration as an infinite proof. Explicit domain: even m>=2, primes p, exponents a>=1, prime-relative density.

evidence: Defant, Theorem 18, quantifies over all even m and all exponents but only asserts infinitely many prime bases with strong abundance.
Defant, Theorems 13–17, concern general deficiency and specific obstructing factors, but do not give an all-prime-base density formula.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 18 is the closest result and its quantification in the exponent is genuinely stronger than any fixed-exponent statement, but its base-prime coverage is only a selected infinite progression. It neither covers all favorable reduced classes nor excludes the unfavorable classes, so it does not imply the stated density by itself. New uniform lower bound and congruence converse supply the missing coverage.

evidence: Defant (2015), Theorem 18 proves an infinite family by CRT plus a prime-divisor product lower bound; its displayed inequality is a sufficient condition for abundance.
The new proof additionally proves a uniform lower bound L_m(u) >= c_m sqrt(u) on every m-rough integer and classifies the bad residue classes by a zero second iterate.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The old theorem implies abundance in at least one progression and gives a model for two-iterate estimates; it does not imply the exact density without covering every favorable progression and ruling out every bad progression. Conversely, the present density claim does not imply the arbitrary polynomial-margin parameter of Theorem 18. The proofs share the known multiplicativity and two-iterate formula, with new universal class coverage and sharp small-m cases.

value.rationale: The full dichotomy computes a natural proportion of prime bases supporting abundance at every exponent, for each even parameter. Unlike mere enumeration or a one-progression existence proof, it determines both favorable and unfavorable congruence regions and identifies finite exceptional bases. The no-exception m=2,4 results completely classify all prime-power inputs in the two first cases and exclude perfect prime powers in those cases. This addresses quantitative distribution and exact structural strata of a previously studied arithmetic iterate sum.
